answer: Random cross-examination: each epoch a beacon picks 5% of identities for a cross-examination. Each locks a 60-credit bond. Examiners wander through its work trail, asking what only its author could answer. Each submission carries a pigment fingerprint, a hash of wording, matching the answers; a mismatch burns the bond. The k-th fake needs its own bond and stand-in, because one operator cannot bridge the canyon between two sessions. 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits plus 1,000 stand-ins. An honest agent pays one bond. Rented answers fail: a stand-in lacks the trail behind the pigment fingerprint.
